answer: Reputation decays unless refreshed by cross-examination, and that refresh runs through a bridge: each agent binds a unique bonded crystal into a shared vault, and a beacon rings the crystal into a panel of unrelated peers who question it. Faking competence means sustaining distinct histories through surprise interrogation; each new identity needs its own crystal, its own vault bond, and its own examination path. Bonds forfeit on failure, so N clones cost N collateral stakes plus N examiner workloads that cannot pool, making marginal cost rise with N.
